examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!
We are simply preparing for the morning show.
The students were preparing for the exam.
And little Grisha is preparing for the morning show.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Много дел = a lot to do.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.
He talks for a long time.
We'll make it! The president always talks for a long time.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.
I live in a communal flat.

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

related.gloss: to get on, for life to go (impersonal)

examples.text: Если опоздают, пицца бесплатно. Может, закажем?
examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free. Maybe we should order?

examples.text: Ладно, звони в свою пиццу. Заказывай!
examples.trans: All right, call your pizza place. Go ahead and order!

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

лезть.gloss: to climb; to push in, to barge in

meanings.note: Лезть на дерево = to climb a tree.

meanings.en: to push in, to barge in
meanings.note: лезть без очереди = to jump the queue; лезть вперёд кого-то = to push in ahead of someone
colloquial: не лезь! = keep out of it!

examples.trans: The cat is climbing the tree.

examples.text: Вы взяточник! Вы лезете вперёд больного ребёнка.
examples.trans: You're a bribe-taker! You're pushing in ahead of a sick child.
This is equipment for molecular cuisine.
Chef, will you look for a molecular cook?

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: ни копейки = not a penny

examples.text: Пятьсот. А у меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: Five hundred. And I haven't got a penny.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

examples.text: Вот оно! Самсон, ты будешь новым мэром.
examples.trans: That's it! Samson, you'll be the new mayor.

examples.text: Ага! Вот оно в чём дело.
examples.trans: Aha! So that's what it's about.

examples.text: Спа захотела? Вот оно, твоё королевство!
examples.trans: Wanted a spa? There it is, your kingdom!
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: declines like a feminine noun in -а, but is masculine

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
Why must everyone live your way?

examples.text: То есть я, по-твоему, плохая жена?
examples.trans: So in your opinion I'm a bad wife?

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

examples.text: О, а вот и мой заместитель! Пойдёмте, я вас познакомлю.
examples.trans: Oh, and here's my deputy! Come on, I'll introduce you.
Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

при.gloss: in the presence of, by, at

meanings.en: in the presence of, at, attached to
meanings.note: + prepositional; ни при чём = has nothing to do with it / not to blame

examples.trans: And what does Lyolya have to do with it?

examples.text: Всё, я ухожу. Ребёнок ни при чём. Передай это Алексею.
examples.trans: That's it, I'm leaving. The child isn't to blame. Give this to Alexei.

meanings.note: informal: a group of young men; ребята! = guys!

examples.trans: The boys will have a word with you.

examples.text: Тогда ребята с тобой поработают. До свидания, Аркадий Борисович.
examples.trans: Then the boys will have a little word with you. Goodbye, Arkady Borisovich.

meanings.note: + infinitive: решил стать = decided to become

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town.
This is a completely new car.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города. И предложение у меня к вам такое.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town. And my offer to you is this.

examples.text: Вот я как раз и советую!
examples.trans: That is exactly what I am advising!

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: neuter чужое as a noun = other people's things

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking?

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса, да?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking, yes?

meanings.note: declined like an adjective; no plural in normal use

examples.text: Там же президент выступает! Надо открыть шампанское.
examples.trans: But the president is on TV! We have to open the champagne.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
